1	# New-Project Bootstrap Path Validation
2	
3	Validate and fix the new-project path where no ARCHITECTURE.md exists. Both MASTER_PROMPTs (web and mobile) have a new-project bootstrap flow that has never been run. Exercise these paths in real new projects, identify failures, and fix them. Ensure dev-skill works from project day one — not just on mature codebases with existing architecture documentation.
4	
5	## Rationale
6	The new-project path is a known gap that has never been tested. For dev-skill to grow beyond its current user base, it must work for developers starting fresh — not just developers adding it to existing projects. This addresses the user goal of having 'a repeatable workflow that works across web, iOS, Android, and KMP projects' including greenfield projects. It also reduces a barrier to adoption for the secondary persona of 'teams adopting AI coding agents.'
7	
8	## User Stories
9	- As a developer starting a new project, I want dev-skill to bootstrap the necessary architecture documentation so that I can use the full pipeline from day one
10	- As a developer, I want the pipeline to handle the absence of ARCHITECTURE.md gracefully rather than failing or producing incorrect results
11	
12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] The web MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new web project
14	- [ ] The mobile MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new mobile project
15	- [ ] ARCHITECTURE.md is generated correctly for new projects with appropriate initial structure
16	- [ ] Discovered issues are fixed and re-validated
17	- [ ] The bootstrap flow works with all supported stacks (Next.js, React, Vue, iOS, Android, KMP)
18

1	# Master Prompt — Web Architecture Strategy (Next.js App Router)
2	
3	> **Use once per project** to lock architecture, conventions, and AI usage rules. Pin decisions in `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the repo root. Per-feature prompts must derive from the rules established here.
4	
5	Use when `package.json` indicates Next.js (App Router). If the project uses a different web stack, adapt accordingly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Goal
10	Design a real-world, scalable Next.js architecture that:
11	- Ships features fast with minimal complexity
12	- Uses server components by default — client components only when necessary
13	- Keeps data flow explicit and ownership clear
14	- Uses AI (Claude Code) as a force multiplier, not a risk
15	
16	Act as a **Senior Web Architect** and provide a **phased implementation plan**. Each phase must include **Goals, Deliverables, Risks, Exit Criteria**.
17	
18	Phases:
19	- **Phase 0 — Validation / POC**
20	- **Phase 1 — Core Architecture Setup**
21	- **Phase 2 — Feature Development**
22	- **Phase 3 — Integrations & Performance**
23	- **Phase 4 — Scale & Maintenance**
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Topics to Cover
28	
29	### 1. App Router Structure
30	- Server vs client component boundaries — when to use `"use client"`
31	- Route organization: `app/[feature]/page.tsx`, `app/[feature]/layout.tsx`
32	- Route groups `(group)/` for shared layouts without URL segments
33	- Loading and error boundaries per route segment
34	
35	### 2. Data Fetching
36	- Server components fetch data directly — no useEffect, no client-side fetching by default
37	- Route Handlers (`app/api/`) only for browser-triggered mutations or external webhooks
38	- Server Actions for form submissions and mutations from client components
39	- File system access (`fs`) — valid in server components, never in client components
40	
41	### 3. State Management
42	- URL state first (`searchParams`, `useRouter`) — survives refresh, shareable
43	- React `useState` for ephemeral UI state (open/closed, current tab)
44	- Zustand or Jotai only if state crosses more than 2 component levels AND cannot be URL state
45	- No Redux — too heavy for Next.js App Router patterns
46	
47	### 4. Styling
48	- Tailwind CSS with CSS variables for theming (`--color-primary`, etc.)
49	- No inline styles except for dynamic values (e.g. calculated widths)
50	- Component variants via `cva` (class-variance-authority) or simple string concatenation
51	- Dark mode via Tailwind `dark:` + `class` strategy on `<html>`
52	
53	### 5. Component Organization
54	```
55	src/
56	├── app/                    ← routes only (page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx)
57	├── components/
58	│   ├── ui/                 ← base components (Button, Card, Input) — no business logic
59	│   └── [feature]/          ← feature-specific components
60	└── lib/
61	    ├── data.ts             ← all data access (fs reads, DB queries, API calls)
62	    └── types.ts            ← shared TypeScript types
63	```
64	
65	### 6. File System Access (local-data apps)
66	- All `fs` reads go in `lib/data.ts` — never scatter them across components
67	- Server components call `lib/data.ts` functions directly
68	- Mutations (writes) go through Server Actions — validates input before writing
69	- Never expose raw file paths to the client
70	
71	### 7. Claude Code Integration Rules
72	- One spec per feature in `specs/[feature-slug].md` before implementation starts
73	- Read `PROJECT_MAP.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` before every session
74	- Propose file changes before writing — no surprises
75	- Server component by default — justify every `"use client"`
76	- No TODOs, no stubs, no placeholders in committed code
77	
78	### 8. Performance
79	- Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms
80	- Use `next/image` for all images
81	- Use `next/font` for all custom fonts (eliminates FOUT)
82	- Minimize client bundle: audit with `@next/bundle-analyzer`
83	- Avoid `"use client"` at layout level — pushes all children into client bundle
84	
85	### 9. Release — pre prod and prod (Vercel)
86	- **Name both environments and the branch that reaches each.** Phase 14 merges to PRE PROD; Phase 16
87	  promotes to PROD. If one branch does both, say so explicitly — that is a single-stage model and
88	  the merge IS the production gate.
89	- **Write the branch model into a release runbook** (`docs/deploy-and-staging.md` or similar). Some
90	  hosts release prod on the merge itself, others need a manual step; getting it wrong means either
91	  reaching production by surprise or believing you released when you didn't.
92	- Environment variables per environment in the Vercel dashboard, mirrored in `.env.local`
93	  (gitignored). **Note which values DIFFER between pre prod and prod** — that difference is exactly
94	  where "verified in pre prod" stops being evidence.
95	- Preview deployments on every PR — use them for review before the pre-prod merge.
96	- Production: `vercel --prod`, or the promotion merge when auto-deploy is wired.
97	- **Migrations reach prod BEFORE the promotion merge**, never after — the merge releases code that
98	  expects the new schema.
99	
100	### 10. Risks

15	Design a real-world, scalable architecture and execution model that:
16	- Ships features fast
17	- Maximizes native platform capabilities
18	- Uses AI (Claude Code) as a force multiplier, not a risk
19	- Keeps complexity visible and ownership clear
20	
21	Act as a **Senior Mobile Architect** and provide a **deep, phased implementation plan**. Each phase must include **Goals, Deliverables, Risks, Exit Criteria**.
22	
23	Phases:
24	- **Phase 0 — Validation / POC**
25	- **Phase 1 — Core Architecture Setup**
26	- **Phase 2 — Feature Development**
27	- **Phase 3 — Native Integrations**
28	- **Phase 4 — Optimization & Scale**
29	
30	Deliverables:
31	- Architecture diagram (text or Mermaid)
32	- Feature development lifecycle
33	- Practical workflow (battle-tested, not theoretical)
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Variant A — iOS only (Swift / SwiftUI)
38	
39	### Context
40	Native iOS app. Heavy use of Claude Code for scaffolding, refactoring, consistency.
41	Strong need to preserve native platform power: SwiftUI, Apple Watch, HealthKit, BackgroundTasks, WidgetKit.
42	
43	### Topics to cover
44	1. **Feature-first modularization** — Swift packages per feature, clear module graph.
45	2. **Architecture** — SwiftUI + `@Observable` view models, navigation patterns, DI.
46	3. **Native integrations** — HealthKit, Apple Watch / WatchConnectivity, BGTasks, Widgets, Push.
47	4. **Data & sync** — local-first (SwiftData / Core Data / GRDB), sync orchestration, conflict resolution.
48	5. **Claude Code integration** — one spec per feature, architecture rules pinned in prompts, code review checklist.
49	6. **Workflow** — spec → contracts → AI scaffold → integrations → QA. Branching, review, CI/CD.
50	7. **Performance** — main-thread budget, Instruments-driven profiling.
51	8. **Scaling** — adding features, onboarding, long-term consistency.
52	9. **Risks** — AI hallucinations, hidden complexity, untested device paths.
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Variant B — Android only (Kotlin / Jetpack Compose)
57	
58	### Context
59	Native Android app. Heavy use of Claude Code for scaffolding, refactoring, consistency.
60	Strong need to preserve native power: Compose, Health Connect / Google Fit, WorkManager, Services, Widgets.
61	
62	### Topics to cover
63	1. **Feature-first modularization** — Gradle module per feature, clear `:core` / `:feature:*` graph.
64	2. **Architecture** — Compose + Jetpack ViewModel, navigation, DI (Hilt/Koin).
65	3. **Native integrations** — Health Connect / Google Fit, WorkManager, foreground services, Widgets, Push.
66	4. **Data & sync** — local-first (Room / SQLDelight / DataStore), sync orchestration, conflict resolution.
67	5. **Claude Code integration** — one spec per feature, architecture rules pinned, code review checklist.
68	6. **Workflow** — spec → contracts → AI scaffold → integrations → QA. Branching, review, CI/CD.
69	7. **Performance** — Macrobenchmark, Perfetto, baseline profiles.
70	8. **Scaling** — adding features, onboarding, long-term consistency.
71	9. **Risks** — AI hallucinations, hidden complexity, background-execution gotchas.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Variant C — iOS + Android + KMP
76	
77	### Context
78	Feature-based **parallel development**: iOS and Android teams work simultaneously on the same features, sharing logic via Kotlin Multiplatform.
79	Tech: Swift/SwiftUI, Kotlin/Jetpack, KMP, Claude Code.
80	Strong need to preserve native power on both sides (Apple Watch + HealthKit, Google Fit / Health Connect, background, real-time, animations).
81	
82	### Topics to cover (in addition to the shared goal)
83	1. **Parallel feature development** — feature squads (not platform silos), ownership, drift prevention.
84	2. **Architecture (feature-first)** — vertical slices; Shared (KMP) = domain, models, validation, API contracts, sync; Native = UI, navigation, permissions, device integrations. Strict KMP boundaries.
85	3. **Native integration strategy** — Apple Watch + HealthKit; Google Fit / Health Connect; permissions; background sync; real-time updates. Bridging pattern: **Native Adapter → KMP Port**.
86	4. **Data & sync** — local-first; high-frequency data (steps, calories, workouts); orchestration & conflict resolution; data ownership (shared vs platform-specific).
87	5. **Claude Code integration** — one shared feature spec; shared acceptance criteria; architecture rules pinned in prompts; AI code review checklist; **no independent generation per platform**.
88	6. **Workflow** — spec → shared contracts → AI scaffold (layer by layer) → native integrations → parity validation → QA. Branching, review, CI/CD with parity tests.
89	7. **Performance** — what stays native; KMP overhead risks; profiling on both platforms.
90	8. **Scaling** — feature addition, onboarding, long-term consistency.
91	9. **Critical risks** — over-reliance on KMP; AI-generated divergence; feature desync; hidden complexity in shared layers.
92	
93	### Final instruction (Variant C)
94	Design with a **strong bias toward native platform quality**, using KMP only where it clearly reduces duplication without introducing complexity, limitations, or platform drift.

85	3. **Native integration strategy** — Apple Watch + HealthKit; Google Fit / Health Connect; permissions; background sync; real-time updates. Bridging pattern: **Native Adapter → KMP Port**.
86	4. **Data & sync** — local-first; high-frequency data (steps, calories, workouts); orchestration & conflict resolution; data ownership (shared vs platform-specific).
87	5. **Claude Code integration** — one shared feature spec; shared acceptance criteria; architecture rules pinned in prompts; AI code review checklist; **no independent generation per platform**.
88	6. **Workflow** — spec → shared contracts → AI scaffold (layer by layer) → native integrations → parity validation → QA. Branching, review, CI/CD with parity tests.
89	7. **Performance** — what stays native; KMP overhead risks; profiling on both platforms.
90	8. **Scaling** — feature addition, onboarding, long-term consistency.
91	9. **Critical risks** — over-reliance on KMP; AI-generated divergence; feature desync; hidden complexity in shared layers.
92	
93	### Final instruction (Variant C)
94	Design with a **strong bias toward native platform quality**, using KMP only where it clearly reduces duplication without introducing complexity, limitations, or platform drift.

2	
3	## Guiding Principles
4	
5	Derived from three operating protocols, plus rules added since. These apply across every phase.
6	
7	| Principle | Source | Rule |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| **Memory Establishment** | Planning Protocol | Maintain `PROJECT_MAP.md` with `TECH_STACK`, `SYSTEM_FLOW`, and `ORPHANS & PENDING`. Read it before acting; update it after. |
10	| **Simplicity First** | Planning Protocol | Propose the simplest solution. Reject unnecessary complexity. 50 lines > 200 lines. |
11	| **Short Documentation** | Golden Rule | One line, **not zero and not a paragraph**. Delete a comment that restates the code or the types; keep one carrying what the signature cannot — precedence, units, a spec quirk. `@param`/`@returns` stay where the repo generates docs from them. |
12	| **Stop on Ambiguity** | Planning Protocol | If requirements are unclear, do not choose a path silently — stop and ask. |
13	| **Prevent Feature Creep** | Planning Protocol | Stick strictly to the requested scope. No additional features. |
14	| **Time Awareness** | Planning Protocol | Specify year+month. Search for latest stable versions before deciding. |
15	| **Goal-Oriented Execution** | Execution Engine | Define success criteria before writing code, and **confirm them after**. Know what "done" looks like. |
16	| **Production-Ready Code** | Execution Engine | No `// TODO`, no placeholders, no stubs. Code must be complete and handle errors. |
17	| **Self-Verification** | Execution Engine | Write automated tests. Do not leave a mess. Ensure no regressions. |
18	| **Live Synchronization** | Execution Engine | Dynamically update `PROJECT_MAP.md`. Move incomplete features to `ORPHANS & PENDING`. |
19	| **Commitment to Flow** | Execution Engine | Every line of code must serve the user journey defined in `SYSTEM_FLOW`. If a line does not, delete it. |
20	| **Surgical Editing** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Touch only what must be touched. Do not reformat adjacent code, rephrase old comments, or fix style you find imperfect — `dev:comment-budget --apply` excepted, per Universal Rules. |
21	| **Style Matching** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Adhere to current code style, even if you find it imperfect. |
22	| **Clean Your Own Mess** | Surgical Editing Protocol | If your edit orphans a function, import, type, or parameter — remove it. |
23	| **Impact Analysis** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Read `PROJECT_MAP.md`. Accurately identify all affected files before editing. |
24	| **Architectural Integrity** | Surgical Editing Protocol | DRY. Reuse shared/core components. Add logging where behavior is non-trivial. |
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Right-Size the Process (read first)
29	
30	The deep phases are for work that earns them. Triage every task into a tier before you start
31	**building**, and say which tier you picked.
32	
33	**Reading the affected file first is part of triage, not a violation of it.** You cannot tell an
34	auth gate from a typo without opening it, and the tier turns on exactly that. A cheap look — read
35	the file, count the referrers — comes before the tier; the investigation proper is still Phase 4.
36	Observed 2026-08-04: a "rename one file" task was Deep the moment the file turned out to be the
37	app-wide auth redirect.
38	
39	| Tier | When | Process |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| **Light** (default) | Small diff, low blast radius, no money/security/migration | Existing test suite + a quick self-review of the diff. NO subagent reviews, NO browser-automation pass, no checklist ceremony. Phase 4 = only as much investigation as the bug demands. |
42	| **Standard** | Multi-file features, user-visible flows | Tests + run the ONE most valuable live check (the bug repro or the new flow), not the full matrix. Self-review; subagent review only if something feels off. |
43	| **Deep** | Money paths, auth/security, migrations, wide refactors, novel-design features — or the developer asks | Maximum **evidence and rigor**: the full evidence ladder, an agent-run checklist, verified AI review, and a security pass. The two fan-outs (Phase 2 explorers, Phase 6 architects) stay **independently conditional** — Deep does not mandate them, and a rename with one obvious shape should skip both. Deep buys care, not agents. |
44	
45	When in doubt between two tiers, pick the lighter one — the developer can always say "go deeper". A slow pipeline that gets skipped protects nothing.
46	
47	**The tier must land in an artifact, not just in chat.** A tier stated once and then scrolled away
48	is not something anyone can hold you to — the same reason Phase 12's output is a required PR
49	section rather than a claim. So it goes in **two** places, every run:
50	
51	- the **response header** (`dev`), or its one-line equivalent (`dev-*` siblings)
52	- the **PR body**, in the `## PIPELINE` section (Phase 14) — next to what was actually run
53	
54	Without it, a reader cannot tell whether a thin verification section means *low risk* or
55	*skipped work*.
56	
57	**Deep tier declares its cost BEFORE spending it.** Deep spawns 2–3 explorer agents (Phase 2),
58	2–3 architect agents (Phase 6) and a review fan-out (Phase 13) — real time, real money. Say what it
59	will cost and get a word first:
60	
61	> "Deep tier: ~3 explorers + ~3 architects + the review fan-out. Go, or lighter?"
62	
63	Never open a fan-out on the developer's behalf and report the bill afterwards. If they say lighter,
64	they are right — the tier is a proposal, not a verdict.
65	
66	**Use the developer as a fast collaborator:** when a blocker is their state (debugger, session, dashboard) or a 30-second human action beats minutes of automation, ask for it immediately and specifically — one sentence, what + why.

70	## Run Mode — automatic, always. Never ask.
71	
72	**Do not ask how the run should proceed.** There is one mode: run straight through. Each phase
73	reports what it did and what it produced, then the next one starts — no *"shall I continue?"*,
74	not once, not per phase.
75	
76	The question used to be asked once per run and it was a tax that bought nothing: the phases that
77	genuinely need the developer are enumerated below and they stop on their own, so the ask only ever
78	delayed work the developer had already approved. Observed 2026-08-04: a mode ask and a Phase 5 ask
79	arrived back to back before a single file changed.
80	
81	### Four gates stop anyway
82	
83	These are **decisions, not steps**, and running automatically never covers a decision:
84	
85	| Phase | Why it cannot be automatic |
86	|---|---|
87	| **5 — Discuss Before Building** | the go-ahead is the developer's by definition; nothing is consent to build |
88	| **6 — Architecture Alternatives** | the approaches genuinely differ — they pick, you recommend |
89	| **14 — merge to pre prod** | the prod decision, made once against the evidence |
90	| **16 — promotion to prod** | never autonomous |
91	
92	**Automatic means "do not ask between mechanical steps." It never means unattended.** The ceremony
93	is skipped, not the judgment.
94	
95	### Rules
96	
97	- **Automatic still reports.** Each phase says what it did and produced — it just does not stop.
98	  Silence is not speed.
99	- **A blocker outranks it.** Ambiguity, a failed gate, a destructive step or a missing decision
100	  stops the run exactly as it always did. Automatic suppresses *"shall I continue?"*, never
101	  *"this needs you."*
102	- **Stepping is available on request, never by default.** "Slow down" / "ask me between phases"
103	  is honoured for the rest of the run — confirm in one line and carry on. Do not offer it.
104	- **Never end a run silently.** Whatever phase you stop at — the last one, a gate, or a blocker —
105	  name the next phase and ask whether to continue. The full rule, which also governs a run that
106	  STARTED mid-pipeline, is in `entry.md` → *Never end silently.*

110	## Phase 0 — Filing (standalone entry only)
111	
112	Creating the work item. Reached ONLY from `dev:create-bug` / `dev:create-issue` /
113	`dev:create-epic` — a `/dev` run never executes it, because by then the item exists. It produces one
114	issue number and stops.
115	
116	### Filing is intake, not work
117	
118	- **Not investigation.** The report describes the symptom; Phase 4 finds the cause. No repro
119	  attempts, no grepping, no reading the handler — a filing door that debugs turns a one-minute
120	  capture into an afternoon, and the item still is not filed.
121	- **Not decomposition.** An epic is filed as ONE issue. Its slices are cut at Phase 5, where context
122	  load, discovery and investigation have actually happened; here they would be imagined.
123	- **Not a branch.** Phase 3 owns branch timing and cuts at the first WRITE. A branch opened here
124	  would pre-commit a decision Phase 5 has not made yet.
125	
126	The whole phase is one turn. If it is taking three, it has become the work.

3	  "description": "# New-Project Bootstrap Path Validation

Validate and fix the new-project path where no ARCHITECTURE.md exists. Both MASTER_PROMPTs (web and mobile) have a new-project bootstrap flow that has never been run. Exercise these paths in real new projects, identify failures, and fix them. Ensure dev-skill works from project day one — not just on mature codebases with existing architecture documentation.

## Rationale
The new-project path is a known gap that has never been tested. For dev-skill to grow beyond its current user base, it must work for developers starting fresh — not just developers adding it to existing projects. This addresses the user goal of having 'a repeatable workflow that works across web, iOS, Android, and KMP projects' including greenfield projects. It also reduces a barrier to adoption for the secondary persona of 'teams adopting AI coding agents.'

## User Stories
- As a developer starting a new project, I want dev-skill to bootstrap the necessary architecture documentation so that I can use the full pipeline from day one
- As a developer, I want the pipeline to handle the absence of ARCHITECTURE.md gracefully rather than failing or producing incorrect results

- [ ] The mobile MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new mobile project

- [ ] Discovered issues are fixed and re-validated
- [ ] The bootstrap flow works with all supported stacks (Next.js, React, Vue, iOS, Android, KMP)

1	---
2	name: dev
3	description: >
4	  Personal developer workflow for features AND bugs on personal projects.
5	  Accepts: GitHub issue URL or number (#123, github.com/.../issues/N), or a plain feature
6	  title / bug description.
7	  Also trigger when user says "start feature", "work on issue", "new branch for",
8	  "investigate this issue", "fix this bug", or pastes a GitHub issue URL.
9	allowed-tools: [gh, git]
10	---
11	
12	# Dev — Personal Workflow
13	
14	GitHub issues, features and bugs for personal projects.
15	
16	The rules below are CLI-agnostic — plain markdown over `git` and `gh`. Only the invocation
17	(`/dev:<door>`), the `.claude-plugin` namespace and `hooks/` are Claude Code's.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Workspace Config
22	
23	**Lives in `~/Developer/skills/dev-skill/shared/entry.md`** — repo auto-detect, pre-prod branch resolution,
24	prod branch resolution, and the single-stage detection. It is shared with every `dev-*` sibling,
25	so it is defined once there and never duplicated here.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Entry 1 — Input Detection & Routing
30	
31	> **Numbering:** these two are ENTRY steps, not pipeline phases. They run before
32	> `shared/pipeline.md` starts, and are numbered separately so they never collide with the
33	> pipeline's own Phase 1 (Context Load). Order is: Entry 1 → Entry 2 → pipeline Phase 1 → Phase 2 → …
34	
35	| Input | Route |
36	|---|---|
37	| **Nothing at all** | **`dev:issues`** — the tracker view, then ask which to start |
38	| `#N`, `github.com/.../issues/N`, GitHub issue URL | **GitHub** flow |
39	| A bare family name — `run`, `prod`, `pre-prod`, `verify`, `docs`, `review`, `comment-budget`, `trim`, `survey`, `arch` | **Confirm the handoff** — see the guard below |
40	| Any other free text | **Generic** flow |
41	
42	### The empty-input row is a guard, not a convenience
43	
44	**2026-08-05 — bare `/dev` had no defined behaviour.** With no empty row, it fell toward "any other
45	free text", whose Entry 2 says *"the argument text is the feature description / seed"* — and with no
46	argument there is no seed. The outcome was whatever got improvised, up to cutting a branch at
47	Phase 3 for a feature nobody asked for.
48	
49	That is the same failure as the one-word guard below, one step further out: the guard catches
50	`/dev run`, and left `/dev` — strictly more ambiguous — unhandled. Routing empty input to the
51	tracker turns the emptiest input into the most useful answer, and `dev:issues` is read-only, so the
52	worst case is now a board instead of a branch.
53	
54	### Guard — a command-shaped argument is not a feature title
55	
56	`/dev` takes no subcommands, so a bare word falls through to "any other free text" and gets read as
57	a **feature name**: `/dev run` would branch `feature/run` and start building a feature called
58	"run". Observed 2026-08-04.
59	
60	Before routing to Generic, STOP if the argument is:
61	
62	- **a family name** — `run`, `prod`, `pre-prod`, `verify`, `docs`, `review`, `comment-budget`, `survey`, `arch`, with or without the
63	  `dev-` prefix. Name the sibling it maps to and confirm:
64	  *"`/dev run` isn't a subcommand — did you mean `/dev:launch`?"*
65	- **a RENAMED family name.** `trim` is still the advertised trigger (*"trim the comments"*) after the
66	  door became `comment-budget` on 2026-09-07, so `/dev trim` must map, not fall through:
67	  *"`/dev trim` isn't a subcommand — did you mean `/dev:comment-budget`?"* A rename that drops the
68	  old name from this guard while leaving it in the triggers turns it into a feature title.
69	- **a single word with no verb and no object** (`deploy`, `test`, `fix`). Far likelier a mistyped
70	  command than a feature brief.
71	
72	Never open a branch on a one-word argument. **Stop on Ambiguity** applies at the front door, not
73	only at Phase 2 — the cheapest place to catch a wrong turn is before the branch exists.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## Entry 2 — Fetch Context
78	
79	### GitHub Issue
80	
81	Auto-detect repo:
82	```bash
83	git remote get-url origin
84	# SSH:   git@github.com:owner/repo.git  → owner/repo
85	# HTTPS: https://github.com/owner/repo  → owner/repo
86	```
87	
88	Fetch issue:
89	```bash
90	gh issue view <N> --json title,body,labels,assignees,milestone
91	```
92	
93	Detect issue type from labels: `bug` → Bug investigation flow; `enhancement` / `feature` → Feature flow.
94	
95	### Generic (feature title)
96	
97	No external fetch. The argument text is the feature description / seed.
98	Read local context: `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/`, `.spec/`.
99	
100	---

1	# dev-skill
2	
3	**From GitHub issue to production, with your coding agent.**
4	
5	A development workflow that investigates problems, plans solutions, writes code, and verifies changes before release. You approve the key decisions: what to build, which approach to take, when to merge, and when to promote to production.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	```bash
10	git clone https://github.com/hasansa007/dev-skill.git && dev-skill/install.sh
11	```
12	
13	This private repository requires GitHub access. The installer links the checkout into existing skill directories for **Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity**, skipping missing directories. It is safe to rerun.
14	
15	Reload skills with `/reload-skills` in Claude Code, or restart your CLI. Check the loaded skill list.
16	
17	## Start a task
18	
19	```text
20	/dev #496
21	/dev fix the course list losing its scroll position
22	```
23	
24	Bare `/dev` shows current issues and suggested next work. Examples use Claude Code syntax; see the guide for other CLIs and dependencies.
25	
26	![The dev workflow, from discovery to production](assets/dev-journey.gif)
27	
28	## Commands
29	
30	### Start or capture work
31	
32	| Command | Purpose |
33	| --- | --- |
34	| `/dev` | Show current issues and suggested next work. |
35	| `/dev <issue or description>` | Start the full development workflow. |
36	| `/dev:create-issue` | File a work item for later. |
37	| `/dev:create-bug` | File a bug report without implementing the fix. |
38	| `/dev:create-epic` | File a parent epic; split it during planning. |
39	| `/dev:issues` | Show current work, next tasks, and statistics. |
40	| `/dev:survey` | Inspect an app and file confirmed findings. |
41	
42	### Continue delivery
43	
44	| Command | Starting point | Result |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| `/dev:verify` | An existing branch | Verification evidence, followed by documentation checks |
47	| `/dev:docs` | A diff | Documentation and decision checks; PR `## DOCS` content |
48	| `/dev:pre-prod` | A branch ready for delivery | PR preparation, review gates, and an approved merge |
49	| `/dev:review` | A PR with feedback | Addressed feedback and a return to the merge stage |
50	| `/dev:prod` | Verified pre-production work | Production checks and an approved promotion |
51	
52	A full `/dev` run includes these stages. You can also invoke them independently for an existing branch, diff, or PR. Verification continues into documentation checks; merges and production promotion require approval. Code review uses the separate `/code-review` integration.
53	
54	### App and maintenance tools
55	
56	| Command | Purpose |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| `/dev:launch` | Build and launch the app. |
59	| `/dev:launch-kill` | Stop this project's servers started by the launch workflow. |
60	| `/dev:shots` | Capture screens from the running app. |
61	| `/dev:comment-budget` | Report comments and docstrings that exceed the documentation budget. Add `--apply` to make changes. |
62	| `/dev:arch` | Generate a diagram tied to verified source locations. Requires Archify. |
63	
64	See [command examples](documentation/COMMANDS.md) for practical usage and handoffs.
65	
66	## Learn more
67	
68	- [User guide](documentation/GUIDE.md) — usage, compatibility, and troubleshooting.
69	- [Workflow](documentation/WORKFLOW.md) — phases, approvals, and known limitations.
70	- [Contributing](documentation/CONTRIBUTING.md) — structure, design rules, and maintenance.

## ✅ Subtask-1-2 Complete!

I've successfully exercised the web MASTER_PROMPT on the new Next.js project and created a comprehensive reproduction document.

### What Was Delivered

**Created:** `test-projects/nextjs-new/REPRODUCTION.md` (458 lines)

The reproduction document includes:

1. **Test Setup** — Verified new project state (no ARCHITECTURE.md, no PROJECT_MAP.md)
2. **Exact Prompt** — Documented the command used to exercise MASTER_PROMPT
3. **Expected Behavior** — Based on web/MASTER_PROMPT.md analysis
4. **Simulated Output** — Complete architecture plan following all MASTER_PROMPT topics
5. **Issues Discovered:**
   - 🔴 **CRITICAL:** MASTER_PROMPT lacks explicit new-project instructions (ambiguous CREATE vs UPDATE)
   - 🟡 **MODERATE:** No guidance on PROJECT_MAP.md handling for new projects
   - 🟢 **MINOR:** No README.md generation mentioned
6. **Questions for Investigation** — 4 specific questions for Phase 2
7. **Summary Table** — Pass/fail results for each aspect

### Key Findings

The main issue identified: **web/MASTER_PROMPT.md says "pin decisions in ARCHITECTURE.md" but doesn't explicitly say to CREATE the file when it doesn't exist.** This ambiguity could cause:
- File-not-found errors
- Architecture generated but not saved
- Output to chat instead of file
- Silent failures

- **Immediate:** Remaining Phase 1 subtasks (iOS and Android reproduction)
- **Phase 2:** Root cause analysis using this reproduction evidence
- **Phase 3:** Fix MASTER_PROMPT with explicit new-project bootstrap instructions

1	# New-Project Bootstrap Path Validation
2	
3	Validate and fix the new-project path where no ARCHITECTURE.md exists. Both MASTER_PROMPTs (web and mobile) have a new-project bootstrap flow that has never been run. Exercise these paths in real new projects, identify failures, and fix them. Ensure dev-skill works from project day one — not just on mature codebases with existing architecture documentation.
4	
5	## Rationale
6	The new-project path is a known gap that has never been tested. For dev-skill to grow beyond its current user base, it must work for developers starting fresh — not just developers adding it to existing projects. This addresses the user goal of having 'a repeatable workflow that works across web, iOS, Android, and KMP projects' including greenfield projects. It also reduces a barrier to adoption for the secondary persona of 'teams adopting AI coding agents.'
7	
8	## User Stories
9	- As a developer starting a new project, I want dev-skill to bootstrap the necessary architecture documentation so that I can use the full pipeline from day one
10	- As a developer, I want the pipeline to handle the absence of ARCHITECTURE.md gracefully rather than failing or producing incorrect results
11	
12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] The web MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new web project
14	- [ ] The mobile MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new mobile project
15	- [ ] ARCHITECTURE.md is generated correctly for new projects with appropriate initial structure
16	- [ ] Discovered issues are fixed and re-validated
17	- [ ] The bootstrap flow works with all supported stacks (Next.js, React, Vue, iOS, Android, KMP)

16	- Ships features fast

40	Native iOS app. Heavy use of Claude Code for scaffolding, refactoring, consistency.

352	
353	1. **Propose the slices in plain language** — with dependencies and the order you would take them.
354	   Each must be **independently shippable**. A slice that cannot reach pre prod without another is
355	   not a slice; fold it into the one it depends on.
356	2. **Wait.** Phase 5 is a stop-gate and filing children is a write.
357	3. **Then file each as its own labelled issue and attach it to the parent:**
358	
359	````bash
360	CHILD=$(gh issue create --title "..." --label "..." --body "..." --json id -q .id)
361	gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<PARENT>/sub_issues -f sub_issue_id="$CHILD"
362	````
363	
364	   **`sub_issue_id` is the node `.id`, never the `number`.** Passing the number fails or silently
365	   attaches the wrong issue, and it is the part of this that bites every time.
366	
367	4. **Never `- [ ]` checkbox lines for slices.** A checklist in the parent body is invisible to every
368	   board query, carries no label, and cannot be worked by `/dev #N`.
369	5. **Continue this run on the FIRST child, and say which.** The parent is a tracker — it takes no
370	   branch and stays open until its children close. Later children are their own `/dev #N` runs: the
371	   sub-issue list IS the queue, it lives on GitHub, and it therefore survives the session that
372	   created it. Nothing about an epic is held in the conversation.

375	
376	**Skip entirely for backend-only work.** When the change adds or alters anything the user sees,
377	settle the design here — before the plan, and long before the build:
378	
379	1. **Does this pattern already exist?** Consistency is weighted heavily: parallel flows should
380	   reuse the same shell, the same CTA verb, and the same dialog SIZE. Find the closest existing
381	   surface and start from it. Actively call out and kill per-flow divergences — a second dialog
382	   footprint for the same job is a bug, not a variation.
383	2. **Reuse the design system, never invent a parallel one.** Use the `frontend-design` skill.
384	3. **Mock anything visually novel and get the mock APPROVED before implementing.** An approved
385	   mock costs minutes to change; a built screen costs hours, and by then it is defended.

1	# Dev Family — Shared Entry Contract
2	
3	Read by `dev` and by every `dev-*` sibling **before anything else**. One source of truth for
4	workspace resolution and for which pipeline sections always load.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Workspace Resolution
9	
10	```
11	GitHub repo: AUTO-DETECTED at runtime via `git remote get-url origin`
12	             Parse SSH (git@github.com:owner/repo.git) or HTTPS (https://github.com/owner/repo)
13	             Strip .git suffix → owner/repo
14	
15	Pre-prod branch: AUTO-DETECTED — never assume. Resolve in this order:
16	  1. The repo's release runbook (`docs/deploy-and-staging.md` or similar) — its
17	     branch model WINS over anything below.
18	  2. First that exists on the remote: `staging` → `develop` → `main` / `master`
19	     git branch -r --format='%(refname:short)'
20	  3. Not a git repo → current HEAD
21	
22	Prod branch: the branch whose merge RELEASES PRODUCTION.
23	  1. The runbook wins.
24	  2. Else `main` / `master`.
25	
26	  Worked example — a two-stage repo: pre prod = `staging`, prod = `main`. A feature PR
27	  based on `main` never deploys; merging to `main` DEPLOYS PROD. Confirm both before acting.
28	```
29	
30	If the two resolve to the same branch, the repo has a **single-stage model**: Phase 14's merge
31	already reaches production. Say so explicitly, and skip Phase 16 — **except its secrets pre-flight**
32	(`shared/prod-secrets.md`), which moves to Phase 14 and runs before that merge. It is bound to the
33	merge that releases production, not to a phase number; skipping it here is how it missed the very
34	incident it was written for.
35	
36	## The resolved repo is a WRITE boundary
37	
38	Reading elsewhere is a mistake; **writing elsewhere is a different category of mistake.** Before any
39	commit, branch, push, PR or merge:
40	
41	1. **State the target repo and branch, by name, before acting** — `owner/repo`, not "the app repo".
42	   A phrase like "the other checkout" is not a repo identifier and cannot be checked.
43	2. **Never write to a repo other than the resolved one without an explicit yes** naming that repo.
44	   Authorization to fix something is not authorization to fix it *anywhere*.
45	3. **Work on a NEW BRANCH, never directly on the main line**, so there is a reviewable object before
46	   anything lands — and **cut it from the pre-prod branch resolved above, not from whatever is
47	   checked out.**
48	
49	A branch cut from another unmerged branch inherits that branch's commits, and they become part of
50	your diff, your PR and your review. Nothing warns you: the name is right, the tests pass, and
51	`git status` reports the branch you are **on**, never the one you came **from**.
52	
53	```bash
54	git fetch origin
55	git log --oneline origin/<pre-prod>..HEAD          # empty = you are AT the base; anything = you are not
56	git switch -c <name> --no-track origin/<pre-prod>  # --no-track matters, see below
57	```
58	
59	**`--no-track` is not optional.** Without it the new branch's upstream is the *base*, and git's first
60	suggestion for a bare `git push` becomes `git push origin HEAD:<pre-prod>` — which lands your commits
61	on the pre-prod branch and skips Phases 12 and 13 entirely. With it, git suggests
62	`--set-upstream origin <name>`, which is what you want. Verified on git 2.50.1.
63	
64	**When the dependency is real** — an epic's slice that needs its sibling's unmerged code — cut from
65	that branch deliberately, say so in the PR body, and target the PR at it. The rule forbids the
66	*accidental* dependency, not the chosen one.
67	
68	> **2026-08-31 — two doors, one base, and a PR that carried the wrong one.** A branch for a new door
69	> was cut while another door's branch was checked out, so it inherited that door's commit. The cost
70	> arrived at the PR: the diff carried the other work, so the PR was targeted at *that* branch to keep
71	> it readable — then that branch moved, the PR went `CONFLICTING`, and the repair was a rebase, a
72	> conflict resolution, a force-push and a retarget. One `--no-track` cut from the base would have
73	> avoided all of it. **Two branches from one base are independent; a branch from a branch is a
74	> dependency nobody agreed to.**
75	
76	> **2026-08-05 → 06 — read-boundary written, write-boundary missing.** A boundary rule was added to
77	> `dev:issues` after it rendered another repo's board — read-only, and the user still had to ask
78	> *"what branch, what repo?"*. Hours later the same session opened and merged **two PRs** into that
79	> other repo on a two-word instruction, without naming the repo first. Both were docs-only; both
80	> reached `main` via a promotion, and in that repo merging to `main` auto-deploys production.
81	>
82	> The first rule was scoped to rendering a board, so it did not cover the case that matters. **A
83	> boundary that only governs reads is not a boundary.** The user's correction was explicit: verify
84	> the origin before changing anything, and at minimum cut a branch.
85	
86	## A result is not a claim — say what it MEANS
87	
88	`dev:launch` 2.0 rule 2 covers the **empty** result: never report absence without printing where you
89	looked. This is its other half, and the harder one. A non-empty result that answers a **narrower
90	question than you asked** is plausible on its face, so nothing prompts a second look — and it gets
91	reported as the broader answer.
92	
93	Before any command's output becomes a claim, check three things:
94	
95	1. **Scope limiter** — does the command bound its own coverage? `-maxdepth`, `head`, `--limit`, a
96	   path prefix, or a regex that **enumerates** cases where it should match a class. If it does:
97	   remove the limit, or report the number as a **floor** and name what bounds it.
98	2. **Ambiguous encoding** — does any output value carry two meanings? A blank field that means both
99	   *"in sync"* and *"not configured"*; a `0` that means both *"none"* and *"not measured"*.
100	   Disambiguate with a second query **before** labelling.

1	# Development workflow
2	
3	The pipeline takes a task through investigation, planning, implementation, verification, documentation, review, and release. Its authoritative procedures live in [`shared/pipeline.md`](../shared/pipeline.md).
4	
5	## Phases
6	
7	| Phase | Stage | Main responsibility |
8	| --- | --- | --- |
9	| 0 | Filing | Draft an issue, resolve labels, and file it. Standalone only. |
10	| 1 | Context | Read project maps, architecture, and existing specifications. |
11	| 2 | Discovery | Identify the stack and perform relevant discovery. |
12	| 3 | Branch naming | Resolve the branch name; create the branch at the first write. |
13	| 4 | Investigation | Follow the evidence ladder; reproduce bugs before theorising. |
14	| 5 | Discussion | Agree on scope and approach before building; split epics when needed. |
15	| 6 | Architecture | Evaluate distinct alternatives when applicable and record rejected options. |
16	| 7 | Plan | Write the implementation plan to `specs/`. |
17	| 8 | Tasks | Break the plan into actionable work. |
18	| 9 | Implementation | Make focused changes using the surgical implementation protocol. |
19	| 10 | Quality checks | Run the project's pre-PR checks. |
20	| 11 | Verification | Collect evidence per checklist item and clean up resources started for verification. |
21	| 12 | Documentation | Check documentation and architecture decisions against the change. |
22	| 13 | Code review | Review the diff; include security review for Deep-tier work. |
23	| 14 | PR and merge | Prepare the PR, satisfy review gates, and obtain merge approval. |
24	| 15 | Review cycle | Address feedback and return to Phase 14. |
25	| 16 | Production | Check secrets and migrations before an approved promotion. |
26	
27	Phase 0 is invoked through filing commands, outside a full `/dev` run. Survey-created issues supply earlier evidence, but Phase 4 still performs investigation layers 3–5.
28	
29	## Decision points
30	
31	The workflow asks before building, when selecting architecture, before merging, and before promoting to production. Other stages normally continue without repeated confirmation.
32	
33	Standalone verification automatically continues into documentation checks. It does not automatically merge or promote the change.
34	
35	## What carries across sessions
36	
37	Planning and implementation depend on the active conversation's reasoning. Later entry points work from persistent artifacts: a branch, diff, or PR. This is why you can invoke verification or review independently.
38	
39	Phase 15 loops back to Phase 14. It does not advance directly to production.
40	
41	## Evidence and documentation
42	
43	- Verification records what was checked, the observed evidence, and any limits.
44	- The PR's `## PIPELINE` section records completed and skipped phases, including reasons.
45	- The PR's `## DOCS` section records documentation and decision checks.
46	- Changed decisions and affected documentation must be accurate before merge.
47	- Teardown must preserve resources the agent did not start.
48	
49	## Release environments
50	
51	[`shared/entry.md`](../shared/entry.md) resolves repository boundaries and branches. In a two-stage repository, Phase 14 reaches pre-production and Phase 16 promotes to production. When both resolve to the same branch, Phase 16 skips a separate promotion.
52	
53	## Known gaps
54	
55	These notes preserve the previous guide's dated validation history. They describe the state at the dates recorded, rather than results from this documentation change.
56	
57	<details>
58	<summary>Validation history and recovery considerations</summary>
59	
60	Honest, as of 2026-08-04:
61	
62	- **Epic support is new and unexercised (2026-08-04).** The design: file the parent with
63	  `/dev:create-epic`, split it at Phase 5 into real sub-issues, run `/dev #child` per slice — the
64	  pipeline stays task-shaped and the sub-issue list is the queue. Never run end to end.
65	- **No rollback — but two thirds of it is mechanical.** It runs 1 → 16 and stops, and nothing
66	  answers *"prod is broken, now what."* Spiked 2026-08-08, and the finding is that this is **not one
67	  gap**. Phase 16 applies schema BEFORE code, so a rollback has to run code-then-schema, and only
68	  the first half reverses:
69	
70	  | Case | Reversible | How |
71	  |---|---|---|
72	  | **Code-only promotion** — no migration in the diff | **yes, always** | revert the promotion merge on the prod branch. Any platform that deploys on merge redeploys on revert — no platform rollback feature is involved |
73	  | **Additive migration** — new nullable column, new table, new index | **yes**, code only | old code ignores the new schema, so leave it forward. Must be *identified*, never assumed |
74	  | **Destructive migration** — drop, rename, narrowing type, overwriting backfill | **no** | the data is already gone. What exists is point-in-time **restore**, which also reverts every unrelated write since. That is not a rollback, and it is never autonomous |
75	
76	  So a `dev:rollback` door's first job is **classification, not execution**: read the promotion
77	  diff, classify each migration, and refuse the third case while naming what a restore would cost.
78	  Phase 16 already computes the input it needs — `git log <prod>..<pre-prod>` — and already requires
79	  migrations applied before the merge, which is exactly what makes the three cases separable.

Perfect! I've successfully completed subtask-2-1. Here's what was accomplished:

## ✅ Subtask-2-1 Complete: Web MASTER_PROMPT Root Cause Analysis

### Created Deliverable
**File:** `test-projects/ROOT_CAUSE_WEB.md` (338 lines, 12KB)

### Key Findings - 5 Critical Gaps Identified

1. **Missing Bootstrap Trigger**
   - SKILL.md says MASTER_PROMPT should apply "when ARCHITECTURE.md is missing"
   - Pipeline Phase 1 checks for ARCHITECTURE.md but doesn't trigger creation
   - No automatic invocation mechanism exists

2. **Ambiguous File Creation**
   - MASTER_PROMPT says "Pin decisions in ARCHITECTURE.md"
   - Doesn't explicitly say "CREATE this file" or provide write instructions
   - Unclear if output should be text response vs actual file creation

3. **Pipeline Asymmetry**
   - PROJECT_MAP.md has fallback: "If absent, create it in Phase 7"
   - ARCHITECTURE.md has NO such fallback
   - Phase 1 loads both but only one has creation logic

4. **Unclear Invocation Model**
   - Documentation conflicts on manual vs automatic invocation
   - No pipeline phase says "run MASTER_PROMPT when missing"

5. **Unvalidated Path**
   - New-project bootstrap flow never tested end-to-end
   - Reproductions show content generation works, but file creation doesn't happen

### Proposed Fixes (4 Concrete Changes)

1. **Phase 2 Bootstrap Trigger** - Add automatic MASTER_PROMPT invocation when ARCHITECTURE.md missing
2. **Explicit File Creation** - Update MASTER_PROMPT header to say "CREATE ARCHITECTURE.md with..."
3. **Phase 1 Fallback** - Add note about Phase 2 bootstrap when ARCHITECTURE.md absent
4. **SKILL.md Clarification** - Document automatic bootstrap vs manual re-architecture

### Evidence Sources
- `./shared/pipeline.md` (Phase 1-2, 7)
- `./SKILL.md` (line 155)
- `./web/MASTER_PROMPT.md` (line 3)
- `./test-projects/nextjs-new/REPRODUCTION.md` (actual behavior)

### Commit
```

According to the implementation plan:
- **subtask-2-2:** Analyze mobile MASTER_PROMPT bootstrap failures
- **subtask-2-3:** Analyze pipeline Phase 1 behavior when ARCHITECTURE.md is missing

The root cause is clear: **MASTER_PROMPT content generation works perfectly (proven by reproductions), but automatic invocation and file persistence are missing from the pipeline.**
I'll analyze the mobile MASTER_PROMPT bootstrap failures and create a root cause analysis. Let me start by examining the spec and any existing evidence.

188	     - Web (Next.js/React/Vue) → `web/MASTER_PROMPT.md`
189	     - Mobile (iOS/Android/KMP) → `mobile/MASTER_PROMPT.md`

192	   - Report: "Created ARCHITECTURE.md for new [stack] project"

Perfect! I've successfully completed subtask-2-2. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

## ✅ Subtask Completed: Mobile MASTER_PROMPT Root Cause Analysis

### What I Did

1. **Analyzed iOS and Android Reproduction Evidence**
   - Reviewed iOS (Variant A) reproduction - 1276 lines of comprehensive architecture
   - Reviewed Android (Variant B) reproduction - 1028 lines of comprehensive architecture
   - Both generated excellent, production-ready content

2. **Created ROOT_CAUSE_MOBILE.md** (652 lines, 23KB)
   - Comprehensive analysis with evidence from both platforms
   - Identified **6 critical gaps** (5 same as web + 1 mobile-specific)
   - Provided detailed proposed fixes with code examples
   - Included validation plan for all three variants (iOS/Android/KMP)

### Key Findings

**Identical to Web (5 gaps):**
1. Missing bootstrap trigger logic
2. Ambiguous file creation instructions
3. Pipeline asymmetry (PROJECT_MAP.md has fallback, ARCHITECTURE.md doesn't)
4. No invocation documentation
5. Unvalidated new-project path

**Mobile-Specific (NEW):**
6. **Variant selection gap** - Pipeline detects iOS/Android/KMP stack but has NO logic to route to correct MASTER_PROMPT variant (A/B/C)

### Critical Insight

Both iOS and Android MASTER_PROMPTs generated **excellent architecture content**:
- iOS: 800+ lines with SwiftUI, SPM modules, HealthKit patterns
- Android: 1000+ lines with Compose, Gradle conventions, Health Connect patterns

**The problem is NOT the content quality - it's WHERE the output goes:**
- ❌ No files created (content only in REPRODUCTION.md)
- ❌ No automatic invocation
- ❌ No variant routing logic

### Proposed Fixes

1. **Add Bootstrap Trigger to Phase 2** - with variant selection logic
2. **Make File Creation Explicit** - remove "e.g." ambiguity
3. **Add Variant Selection Documentation** - clarify automatic vs manual
4. **Add ARCHITECTURE.md Fallback to Phase 1** - set expectations

### Next Steps

This completes Phase 2 investigation. The next subtask (2-3) will analyze pipeline Phase 1 behavior, then Phase 3 will implement the fixes across all prompts.

**Files Changed:**
- ✅ Created: `test-projects/ROOT_CAUSE_MOBILE.md`
- ✅ Updated: `implementation_plan.json` (marked subtask-2-2 as completed)
- ✅ Committed with descriptive message

## ✅ Subtask-2-3 Complete: Pipeline Phase 1 Root Cause Analysis

### What Was Created

**`test-projects/ROOT_CAUSE_PIPELINE.md`** — A comprehensive 660-line analysis documenting how pipeline Phase 1 (Context Load) fails to gracefully handle new projects.

### Key Findings

Identified **5 critical asymmetries** in Phase 1:

1. **Silent failure mode** — When ARCHITECTURE.md is missing, Phase 1 triggers no action (just silently continues)

2. **Asymmetric fallback logic** — PROJECT_MAP.md has explicit creation fallback ("If absent, create it in Phase 7"), but ARCHITECTURE.md has none

3. **No new-project detection** — Phase 1 can't distinguish between:
   - New project (both files missing) → needs bootstrap
   - Broken project (PROJECT_MAP.md exists, ARCHITECTURE.md missing) → needs recovery

4. **Optimistic reporting** — Report template assumes success case only ("Loaded PROJECT_MAP + ARCHITECTURE") with no examples for partial/missing states

5. **Guiding Principles gap** — ARCHITECTURE.md not elevated to same foundational status as PROJECT_MAP.md in the "Memory Establishment" principle

### Proposed Solutions

Four concrete fixes documented:

1. **Add new-project detection** to Phase 1 (check both context files, report state clearly)
2. **Update reporting** to handle all states (new/partial/full context)
3. **Add Phase 1.5 bootstrap hook** or extend Phase 2 with bootstrap trigger
4. **Elevate ARCHITECTURE.md** in Guiding Principles to match PROJECT_MAP.md status

### Integration with Other Analyses

This completes the **3-part integration** identified across all root cause analyses:

- **Phase 1 (Detection)** ← This analysis: Detect new projects when both context files missing
- **Phase 2 (Bootstrap)** ← Web/mobile analyses: Auto-generate ARCHITECTURE.md with appropriate MASTER_PROMPT variant
- **MASTER_PROMPT (Clarity)** ← Web/mobile analyses: Make file creation explicit instead of implied

All three Phase 2 subtasks are now done:
- ✅ subtask-2-1: Web root cause analysis
- ✅ subtask-2-2: Mobile root cause analysis

1	# Master Prompt — Web Architecture Strategy (Next.js App Router)
2	
3	> **Use once per project** to lock architecture, conventions, and AI usage rules. Pin decisions in `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the repo root. Per-feature prompts must derive from the rules established here.
4	
5	Use when `package.json` indicates Next.js (App Router). If the project uses a different web stack, adapt accordingly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Goal
10	Design a real-world, scalable Next.js architecture that:
11	- Ships features fast with minimal complexity
12	- Uses server components by default — client components only when necessary
13	- Keeps data flow explicit and ownership clear
14	- Uses AI (Claude Code) as a force multiplier, not a risk
15	
16	Act as a **Senior Web Architect** and provide a **phased implementation plan**. Each phase must include **Goals, Deliverables, Risks, Exit Criteria**.
17	
18	Phases:
19	- **Phase 0 — Validation / POC**
20	- **Phase 1 — Core Architecture Setup**
21	- **Phase 2 — Feature Development**
22	- **Phase 3 — Integrations & Performance**
23	- **Phase 4 — Scale & Maintenance**
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Topics to Cover
28	
29	### 1. App Router Structure
30	- Server vs client component boundaries — when to use `"use client"`
31	- Route organization: `app/[feature]/page.tsx`, `app/[feature]/layout.tsx`
32	- Route groups `(group)/` for shared layouts without URL segments
33	- Loading and error boundaries per route segment
34	
35	### 2. Data Fetching
36	- Server components fetch data directly — no useEffect, no client-side fetching by default
37	- Route Handlers (`app/api/`) only for browser-triggered mutations or external webhooks
38	- Server Actions for form submissions and mutations from client components
39	- File system access (`fs`) — valid in server components, never in client components
40	
41	### 3. State Management
42	- URL state first (`searchParams`, `useRouter`) — survives refresh, shareable
43	- React `useState` for ephemeral UI state (open/closed, current tab)
44	- Zustand or Jotai only if state crosses more than 2 component levels AND cannot be URL state
45	- No Redux — too heavy for Next.js App Router patterns
46	
47	### 4. Styling
48	- Tailwind CSS with CSS variables for theming (`--color-primary`, etc.)
49	- No inline styles except for dynamic values (e.g. calculated widths)
50	- Component variants via `cva` (class-variance-authority) or simple string concatenation
51	- Dark mode via Tailwind `dark:` + `class` strategy on `<html>`
52	
53	### 5. Component Organization
54	```
55	src/
56	├── app/                    ← routes only (page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx)
57	├── components/
58	│   ├── ui/                 ← base components (Button, Card, Input) — no business logic
59	│   └── [feature]/          ← feature-specific components
60	└── lib/
61	    ├── data.ts             ← all data access (fs reads, DB queries, API calls)
62	    └── types.ts            ← shared TypeScript types
63	```
64	
65	### 6. File System Access (local-data apps)
66	- All `fs` reads go in `lib/data.ts` — never scatter them across components
67	- Server components call `lib/data.ts` functions directly
68	- Mutations (writes) go through Server Actions — validates input before writing
69	- Never expose raw file paths to the client
70	
71	### 7. Claude Code Integration Rules
72	- One spec per feature in `specs/[feature-slug].md` before implementation starts
73	- Read `PROJECT_MAP.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` before every session
74	- Propose file changes before writing — no surprises
75	- Server component by default — justify every `"use client"`
76	- No TODOs, no stubs, no placeholders in committed code
77	
78	### 8. Performance
79	- Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms
80	- Use `next/image` for all images
81	- Use `next/font` for all custom fonts (eliminates FOUT)
82	- Minimize client bundle: audit with `@next/bundle-analyzer`
83	- Avoid `"use client"` at layout level — pushes all children into client bundle
84	
85	### 9. Release — pre prod and prod (Vercel)
86	- **Name both environments and the branch that reaches each.** Phase 14 merges to PRE PROD; Phase 16
87	  promotes to PROD. If one branch does both, say so explicitly — that is a single-stage model and
88	  the merge IS the production gate.
89	- **Write the branch model into a release runbook** (`docs/deploy-and-staging.md` or similar). Some
90	  hosts release prod on the merge itself, others need a manual step; getting it wrong means either
91	  reaching production by surprise or believing you released when you didn't.
92	- Environment variables per environment in the Vercel dashboard, mirrored in `.env.local`
93	  (gitignored). **Note which values DIFFER between pre prod and prod** — that difference is exactly
94	  where "verified in pre prod" stops being evidence.
95	- Preview deployments on every PR — use them for review before the pre-prod merge.
96	- Production: `vercel --prod`, or the promotion merge when auto-deploy is wired.
97	- **Migrations reach prod BEFORE the promotion merge**, never after — the merge releases code that
98	  expects the new schema.
99	
100	### 10. Risks
101	- **Server/client boundary confusion** — component marked `"use client"` that imports a server-only module (crashes at runtime)
102	- **Over-fetching on server** — fetching more data than the component renders
103	- **State sync issues** — mixing URL state, React state, and server state for the same value
104	- **Bundle bloat** — large client-side libraries imported in a server component that got marked `"use client"`
105	- **AI-generated client sprawl** — Claude adding `"use client"` to silence TypeScript errors instead of fixing the real issue
106

1	# Dev Pipeline — Shared Phases
2	
3	## Guiding Principles
4	
5	Derived from three operating protocols, plus rules added since. These apply across every phase.
6	
7	| Principle | Source | Rule |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| **Memory Establishment** | Planning Protocol | Maintain `PROJECT_MAP.md` with `TECH_STACK`, `SYSTEM_FLOW`, and `ORPHANS & PENDING`. Read it before acting; update it after. |
10	| **Simplicity First** | Planning Protocol | Propose the simplest solution. Reject unnecessary complexity. 50 lines > 200 lines. |
11	| **Short Documentation** | Golden Rule | One line, **not zero and not a paragraph**. Delete a comment that restates the code or the types; keep one carrying what the signature cannot — precedence, units, a spec quirk. `@param`/`@returns` stay where the repo generates docs from them. |
12	| **Stop on Ambiguity** | Planning Protocol | If requirements are unclear, do not choose a path silently — stop and ask. |
13	| **Prevent Feature Creep** | Planning Protocol | Stick strictly to the requested scope. No additional features. |
14	| **Time Awareness** | Planning Protocol | Specify year+month. Search for latest stable versions before deciding. |
15	| **Goal-Oriented Execution** | Execution Engine | Define success criteria before writing code, and **confirm them after**. Know what "done" looks like. |
16	| **Production-Ready Code** | Execution Engine | No `// TODO`, no placeholders, no stubs. Code must be complete and handle errors. |
17	| **Self-Verification** | Execution Engine | Write automated tests. Do not leave a mess. Ensure no regressions. |
18	| **Live Synchronization** | Execution Engine | Dynamically update `PROJECT_MAP.md`. Move incomplete features to `ORPHANS & PENDING`. |
19	| **Commitment to Flow** | Execution Engine | Every line of code must serve the user journey defined in `SYSTEM_FLOW`. If a line does not, delete it. |
20	| **Surgical Editing** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Touch only what must be touched. Do not reformat adjacent code, rephrase old comments, or fix style you find imperfect — `dev:comment-budget --apply` excepted, per Universal Rules. |
21	| **Style Matching** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Adhere to current code style, even if you find it imperfect. |
22	| **Clean Your Own Mess** | Surgical Editing Protocol | If your edit orphans a function, import, type, or parameter — remove it. |
23	| **Impact Analysis** | Surgical Editing Protocol | Read `PROJECT_MAP.md`. Accurately identify all affected files before editing. |
24	| **Architectural Integrity** | Surgical Editing Protocol | DRY. Reuse shared/core components. Add logging where behavior is non-trivial. |
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Right-Size the Process (read first)
29	
30	The deep phases are for work that earns them. Triage every task into a tier before you start
31	**building**, and say which tier you picked.
32	
33	**Reading the affected file first is part of triage, not a violation of it.** You cannot tell an
34	auth gate from a typo without opening it, and the tier turns on exactly that. A cheap look — read
35	the file, count the referrers — comes before the tier; the investigation proper is still Phase 4.
36	Observed 2026-08-04: a "rename one file" task was Deep the moment the file turned out to be the
37	app-wide auth redirect.
38	
39	| Tier | When | Process |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| **Light** (default) | Small diff, low blast radius, no money/security/migration | Existing test suite + a quick self-review of the diff. NO subagent reviews, NO browser-automation pass, no checklist ceremony. Phase 4 = only as much investigation as the bug demands. |
42	| **Standard** | Multi-file features, user-visible flows | Tests + run the ONE most valuable live check (the bug repro or the new flow), not the full matrix. Self-review; subagent review only if something feels off. |
43	| **Deep** | Money paths, auth/security, migrations, wide refactors, novel-design features — or the developer asks | Maximum **evidence and rigor**: the full evidence ladder, an agent-run checklist, verified AI review, and a security pass. The two fan-outs (Phase 2 explorers, Phase 6 architects) stay **independently conditional** — Deep does not mandate them, and a rename with one obvious shape should skip both. Deep buys care, not agents. |
44	
45	When in doubt between two tiers, pick the lighter one — the developer can always say "go deeper". A slow pipeline that gets skipped protects nothing.
46	
47	**The tier must land in an artifact, not just in chat.** A tier stated once and then scrolled away
48	is not something anyone can hold you to — the same reason Phase 12's output is a required PR
49	section rather than a claim. So it goes in **two** places, every run:
50	
51	- the **response header** (`dev`), or its one-line equivalent (`dev-*` siblings)
52	- the **PR body**, in the `## PIPELINE` section (Phase 14) — next to what was actually run
53	
54	Without it, a reader cannot tell whether a thin verification section means *low risk* or
55	*skipped work*.
56	
57	**Deep tier declares its cost BEFORE spending it.** Deep spawns 2–3 explorer agents (Phase 2),
58	2–3 architect agents (Phase 6) and a review fan-out (Phase 13) — real time, real money. Say what it
59	will cost and get a word first:
60	
61	> "Deep tier: ~3 explorers + ~3 architects + the review fan-out. Go, or lighter?"
62	
63	Never open a fan-out on the developer's behalf and report the bill afterwards. If they say lighter,
64	they are right — the tier is a proposal, not a verdict.
65	
66	**Use the developer as a fast collaborator:** when a blocker is their state (debugger, session, dashboard) or a 30-second human action beats minutes of automation, ask for it immediately and specifically — one sentence, what + why.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Run Mode — automatic, always. Never ask.
71	
72	**Do not ask how the run should proceed.** There is one mode: run straight through. Each phase
73	reports what it did and what it produced, then the next one starts — no *"shall I continue?"*,
74	not once, not per phase.
75	
76	The question used to be asked once per run and it was a tax that bought nothing: the phases that
77	genuinely need the developer are enumerated below and they stop on their own, so the ask only ever
78	delayed work the developer had already approved. Observed 2026-08-04: a mode ask and a Phase 5 ask
79	arrived back to back before a single file changed.
80	
81	### Four gates stop anyway
82	
83	These are **decisions, not steps**, and running automatically never covers a decision:
84	
85	| Phase | Why it cannot be automatic |
86	|---|---|
87	| **5 — Discuss Before Building** | the go-ahead is the developer's by definition; nothing is consent to build |
88	| **6 — Architecture Alternatives** | the approaches genuinely differ — they pick, you recommend |
89	| **14 — merge to pre prod** | the prod decision, made once against the evidence |
90	| **16 — promotion to prod** | never autonomous |
91	
92	**Automatic means "do not ask between mechanical steps." It never means unattended.** The ceremony
93	is skipped, not the judgment.
94	
95	### Rules
96	
97	- **Automatic still reports.** Each phase says what it did and produced — it just does not stop.
98	  Silence is not speed.
99	- **A blocker outranks it.** Ambiguity, a failed gate, a destructive step or a missing decision
100	  stops the run exactly as it always did. Automatic suppresses *"shall I continue?"*, never

100	### 10. New-Project Bootstrap
101	
102	When setting up a new Next.js project for the first time:
103	
104	#### Path Validation & Project Structure
105	- **Validate the project root path before any file operations** — check it exists and is writable before creating directories or files
106	- **Use `path.resolve()` to normalize all paths** — prevents issues with relative paths, symlinks, and trailing slashes
107	- **Verify parent directory exists before creating nested structures** — failing early prevents partial directory creation
108	- Never assume default locations (`~/projects`, `/Users/...`) — always resolve from the actual working directory
109	
110	#### Bootstrap Sequence
111	1. **Validate target directory** — must exist, must be empty or explicitly confirmed for overwrite, must be writable
112	2. **Create core directories in dependency order:**
113	   ```
114	   src/app/           ← create first (Next.js requires this)
115	   src/components/ui/ ← then UI base components
116	   src/lib/           ← then shared utilities
117	   ```
118	3. **Initialize config files** — `next.config.js`, `tailwind.config.js`, `tsconfig.json` with project-specific settings
119	4. **Install dependencies** — `package.json` first, then `npm install` (or equivalent)
120	5. **Verify bootstrap succeeded** — check all expected directories and files exist before reporting success
121	
122	#### Common Bootstrap Failures
123	- **Invalid path passed to bootstrap** — always resolve and validate before use; error message must show the invalid path
124	- **Partial directory creation** — if any step fails, report exactly which directories were created and which failed
125	- **Silent path resolution failures** — never fall back to current directory silently; make path resolution explicit and loud
126	- **Missing parent directories** — bootstrap should fail fast if the target parent doesn't exist, not attempt to create it
127	
128	#### Anti-Patterns
129	- **Do not create directories outside the project root** — bootstrap is scoped to one project; paths that escape it are bugs
130	- **Do not skip path validation "to save time"** — invalid paths detected at file-write time have already created partial state

1	# Master Prompt — Mobile Architecture Strategy
2	
3	> **Conditional use.** Pick the variant that matches the project. If the stack does not match any variant below, **do not use this prompt**.
4	
5	Use **once per project** to lock architecture, conventions, and AI usage rules. Pin the resulting decisions in the repo (e.g. `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `/specs/`, `/tools/claude-prompts/ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md`). Per-feature prompts must derive from the rules established here.
6	
7	Detect stack from Phase 2 of the pipeline:
8	- `*.xcodeproj` / `Package.swift` (Swift) only → **Variant A — iOS-only**
9	- `build.gradle*` + Android manifest only → **Variant B — Android-only**
10	- `androidApp/` + `iOSApp/` + `shared/` (KMP) → **Variant C — iOS + Android + KMP**
11

13	
14	## Shared Goal (all variants)
15	Design a real-world, scalable architecture and execution model that:
16	- Ships features fast
17	- Maximizes native platform capabilities
18	- Uses AI (Claude Code) as a force multiplier, not a risk
19	- Keeps complexity visible and ownership clear
20	
21	Act as a **Senior Mobile Architect** and provide a **deep, phased implementation plan**. Each phase must include **Goals, Deliverables, Risks, Exit Criteria**.
22	
23	Phases:
24	- **Phase 0 — Validation / POC**
25	- **Phase 1 — Core Architecture Setup**
26	- **Phase 2 — Feature Development**
27	- **Phase 3 — Native Integrations**
28	- **Phase 4 — Optimization & Scale**

31	- Architecture diagram (text or Mermaid)
32	- Feature development lifecycle
33	- Practical workflow (battle-tested, not theoretical)

36	
37	## Variant A — iOS only (Swift / SwiftUI)
38	
39	### Context
40	Native iOS app. Heavy use of Claude Code for scaffolding, refactoring, consistency.
41	Strong need to preserve native platform power: SwiftUI, Apple Watch, HealthKit, BackgroundTasks, WidgetKit.
42

44	1. **Feature-first modularization** — Swift packages per feature, clear module graph.
45	2. **Architecture** — SwiftUI + `@Observable` view models, navigation patterns, DI.

48	5. **Claude Code integration** — one spec per feature, architecture rules pinned in prompts, code review checklist.
49	6. **Workflow** — spec → contracts → AI scaffold → integrations → QA. Branching, review, CI/CD.
50	7. **Performance** — main-thread budget, Instruments-driven profiling.
51	8. **Scaling** — adding features, onboarding, long-term consistency.
52	9. **Risks** — AI hallucinations, hidden complexity, untested device paths.

57	
58	### Context
59	Native Android app. Heavy use of Claude Code for scaffolding, refactoring, consistency.
60	Strong need to preserve native power: Compose, Health Connect / Google Fit, WorkManager, Services, Widgets.
61	
62	### Topics to cover
63	1. **Feature-first modularization** — Gradle module per feature, clear `:core` / `:feature:*` graph.
64	2. **Architecture** — Compose + Jetpack ViewModel, navigation, DI (Hilt/Koin).
65	3. **Native integrations** — Health Connect / Google Fit, WorkManager, foreground services, Widgets, Push.
66	4. **Data & sync** — local-first (Room / SQLDelight / DataStore), sync orchestration, conflict resolution.
67	5. **Claude Code integration** — one spec per feature, architecture rules pinned, code review checklist.

157	### Rules
158	
159	- **One item per invocation.** Three problems in one description are three issues — say so and ask
160	  which to file, or file the first and name the rest. Silently folding them into one produces the
161	  issue that later gets half-closed.
162	- **The type is a default, not a contract.** `dev:create-bug` pointed at something plainly a feature
163	  files a feature and says so. Stop on Ambiguity outranks the door you came through.
164	- **These issues never auto-close** — `Closes #N` does not fire in a repo whose feature PRs target
165	  pre prod. `dev:prod` → *Next* offers the write-back; that is where they close.
166	
167	> The per-type templates live in the three `dev:create-*` members — that is the only thing that
168	> differs between them, and it is the only thing they hold.

1	# New-Project Bootstrap Path Validation
2	
3	Validate and fix the new-project path where no ARCHITECTURE.md exists. Both MASTER_PROMPTs (web and mobile) have a new-project bootstrap flow that has never been run. Exercise these paths in real new projects, identify failures, and fix them. Ensure dev-skill works from project day one — not just on mature codebases with existing architecture documentation.
4	
5	## Rationale
6	The new-project path is a known gap that has never been tested. For dev-skill to grow beyond its current user base, it must work for developers starting fresh — not just developers adding it to existing projects. This addresses the user goal of having 'a repeatable workflow that works across web, iOS, Android, and KMP projects' including greenfield projects. It also reduces a barrier to adoption for the secondary persona of 'teams adopting AI coding agents.'

9	- As a developer starting a new project, I want dev-skill to bootstrap the necessary architecture documentation so that I can use the full pipeline from day one

13	- [ ] The web MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new web project
14	- [ ] The mobile MASTER_PROMPT new-project path has been exercised in a real new mobile project
